What changed in each release of openvireo-core and its bindings. The core follows
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org): a minor release adds API, a patch release fixes or repackages,
and only a major release removes or changes API. Every binding has the core's version.

## 1.2.2

2026-11-28

- **Rust**: the crates are renamed `openvireo-*` (`openvireo-core`, `openvireo-share`, ...) ahead of
  crates.io. Library names stay `ov_*`, so code doesn't change, but a git dependency names the new package:
  `openvireo-core = { git = "https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core", tag = "v1.2.2" }`.
- **npm**: `@openvireo/core-wasm` publishes to npmjs.com by trusted publishing, with no token.
- No API changes.

## 1.2.1

2026-11-28

The same library as 1.2.0, released to the public registries for the first time:

- **Python**: `openvireo` on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/openvireo/).
- **Kotlin / Java**: `com.openvireo:openvireo-core-jvm` and `com.openvireo:openvireo-core-android` on Maven
  Central, with no token.
- **Swift**: the [openvireo-swift](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-swift) package, tagged `1.2.1`.
- **TypeScript**: `@openvireo/core-wasm` on npmjs.com.

## 1.2.0

2026-11-24

- **Added** `ov connect`: the REST server for one service account, now built into the native `ov`. It
  replaces the TypeScript `openvireo-connect` binaries. Container image
  `ghcr.io/openvireo/openvireo-connect`, with a Helm chart and kustomize manifests in `deploy/connect`.
- Contract v1.10: the HTTP server crates behind `ov connect`.
- Docs: a guide for using the core directly from Rust.

## 1.1.0

2026-11-23

- **C++**: `parse_share_link`.
- **Swift**: the released `OpenVireoRustCore.swift` includes the `OvError` field extension (`code`,
  `wireCode`, ...), so apps no longer copy it in.

## 1.0.0

2026-11-22

The first release of the shared Rust core behind the iOS, desktop and web apps, the SDK and `ov`.

- The facade: `OvClient`, `Account`, `Vault`, `ServiceAccount`, `SelfHosted`, the records and `OvError`
  (contract v1.9, which adds `Platform::Android`).
- Bindings: Swift (UniFFI), C++ (cxx), TypeScript (wasm), Python and Kotlin / Java for the JVM and Android.
- The native `ov` CLI, replacing the TypeScript one.
- Faster KDBX: a 5,000-entry merge in 31 ms (was 138 ms), reads in 60 ms, writes in 42 ms.
- KDBX key derivation settings over the limits are refused (`too_large`) before they run.
- Signed release artifacts: Apple notarization, Azure signing and a GPG-signed `SHA256SUMS`.
